chunks: First: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from al-Qasim from Jarrah al-Mada'ini said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a father giving a gift to his child while distinguishing one from the others. He said: If he gives it to him while healthy, it is valid.

Second: As for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah: I asked him about a father giving a gift to his child while distinguishing one. He said: If he is healthy, it is for him to do with it as he wishes. But if he is ill, it is not valid. The explanation for this report is one of two things: One is that it is disliked, and the reason for the dislike is that if he has children and singles out one of them with a gift, it is a concealment/diminution for the others. The other explanation is that it is not valid if he does not distinguish it from his wealth and hand it over to him, for if it is so, it is not permissible unless it is in a manner that makes it like the others, as we have mentioned. And that which indicates the permissibility of preferring some children over others.

Third: What Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man who has children from different mothers, can he prefer some of them over others? He said: There is no harm. Hariz said: Mu'awiya and Abu Kahmas told me that they heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Ali (peace be upon him) did that with his son al-Hasan, and al-Husayn did that with his son Ali (peace be upon him), and my father did it with me, and I did it.

Fourth: From him (Al-Husayn) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who singles out some of his children with some of his wealth, he said: There is no harm with that.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a father to give a gift to one child while excluding others?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the jurisprudential ruling on *tafdil* (favoring one child over another in gifts), establishing its permissibility during both health and illness, contrary to some views that deem it disliked in sickness to prevent sibling rivalry. The text reinforces this by citing the prophetic practice of the Imams, specifically Ali, Hasan, and Husayn, who individually favored their children, thereby providing a strong precedent for unilateral parental discretion in gift-giving prior to inheritance distribution.
